reference: Dead spot? Slide the phone a hand's width, and it can come back. Why? The radio wave arrives by several paths, bouncing off walls. The echoes arrive out of sync. Here they add up, there they cancel. At Bluetooth's two point four gigahertz, one wave is about twelve centimetres long. So weak and strong spots can be just centimetres apart. When a nearby link stalls, shift the phone a little before giving up. Try Meshline for private nearby messaging, even offline.
